steps.tx: Implant-based breast reconstruction accounts for the majority of post-mastectomy reconstructions globally, offered as either immediate or delayed procedures. Techniques are broadly categorized into **two-stage reconstruction** utilizing a temporary tissue expander followed by permanent implant exchange, or single-stage direct-to-implant reconstruction in carefully selected patients.
steps.say: Most breasts rebuilt after mastectomy are rebuilt with implants, either straight away or later. The classic route fills a temporary expander over weeks and then swaps it for the permanent implant, while well-chosen patients with healthy skin flaps can receive the final implant in a single direct operation.

nodes.label: Mastectomy with evaluation of skin flap perfusion
Subpectoral or prepectoral pocket creation with ADM
Tissue expander inflation or direct-to-implant placement

steps.tx: The surgical pocket plane has evolved from total submuscular coverage to **prepectoral reconstruction**. In prepectoral implant placement, the prosthesis resides entirely superficial to the pectoralis major muscle, completely wrapped with an acellular dermal matrix sheet to eliminate animation deformity and decrease postoperative muscle spasm pain.
steps.say: Where the implant sits has moved over the years. Prepectoral reconstruction places it entirely in front of the pectoralis muscle, wrapped completely in acellular dermal matrix, so the breast no longer jumps when the muscle flexes and the patient escapes the ache of a stretched muscle.

left.title: Subpectoral Pocket
points: Implant placed deep to pectoralis major

steps.tx: An **acellular dermal matrix** or ADM provides vital lower pole structural support, acting as an internal sling between the inframammary fold and pectoralis major muscle edge. ADMs control the position of the inframammary fold, provide predictable soft tissue coverage, and reduce the risk of capsular contracture.
steps.say: That dermal matrix acts as an internal bra. Stitched between the chest wall fold and the muscle edge, it holds up the lower pole, pins the inframammary fold exactly where it belongs, gives reliable soft tissue cover, and measurably lowers capsular contracture.

vis.alt: Surgical needle holder for suturing acellular dermal matrix
vis.caption: Surgical instruments utilized in securing the dermal matrix sling to the chest wall. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The Baker classification categorises **capsular contracture** into four progressive grades. Grade I describes a completely natural, soft breast without visible distortion; Grade II is slightly firm to palpation; Grade III is noticeably firm with abnormal contour distortion; Grade IV presents with severe hardness, marked distortion, and persistent breast pain.
steps.say: Baker graded the hardening that can spoil an implant from one to four. One feels soft and looks natural, two is slightly firm, three is firm with a distorted shape, and four is hard, misshapen and painful, which is the grade that earns a capsulectomy.

steps.tx: The pathogenesis of capsular contracture is strongly driven by subclinical bacterial **biofilm formation**, particularly involving Staphylococcus epidermidis. Proven preventative measures include the Adams 14-point plan: triple-antibiotic pocket irrigation, Keller funnel non-touch delivery, meticulous hemostasis, change of surgical gloves, and avoiding peri-areolar incisions.
steps.say: Contracture starts with invisible bacterial biofilm, usually skin staphylococci, filming the implant. The Adams fourteen-point plan fights it: triple-antibiotic wash of the pocket, a Keller funnel so nothing touches the implant, fresh gloves, dry haemostasis, and no incision around the areola.

nodes.label: Subclinical biofilm formation on implant surface

steps.tx: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma or **BIA-ALCL** is an uncommon peripheral T-cell lymphoma that stains strongly positive for CD30 and consistently negative for ALK protein. It is epidemiologically linked almost exclusively to textured implant surfaces with high surface macrotexture and microtexture roughness.
steps.say: Textured implants carry a rare lymphoma of their own. BIA-ALCL is a T-cell lymphoma that stains positive for CD30 and negative for ALK, and it clusters almost entirely around rough macrotextured surfaces rather than smooth ones.

steps.tx: BIA-ALCL presents classically as a spontaneous, painless **delayed seroma** developing 8 to 10 years following initial implant placement. Diagnostic protocol mandates ultrasound-guided aspiration of peri-implant fluid for cytopathology, CD30 immunohistochemistry, and flow cytometry. Mammography alone is inadequate for detecting early periprosthetic effusions.
steps.say: Suspect it when a painless swelling appears eight to ten years after implantation, which is a delayed seroma around the implant. Ultrasound-guided aspiration of that fluid for cytology, CD30 staining and flow cytometry makes the diagnosis, because a mammogram cannot see an early effusion.

vis.alt: Surgical fluid aspiration drain for peri-implant effusion
vis.caption: Surgical effusion drainage and diagnostic fluid collection in implant complications. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Definitive curative treatment for localized BIA-ALCL is complete **en bloc capsulectomy** with removal of the breast implant and excision of any associated capsule mass with clear oncological margins. Partial capsulectomy leaves residual neoplastic clones and leads to significantly higher disease recurrence.
steps.say: Localised disease is cured by taking everything out in one piece: the implant plus the entire capsule and any lump, with clear margins, which is the en bloc capsulectomy. Leaving shreds of capsule behind leaves malignant clones behind and invites the lymphoma back.

left.title: Complete En Bloc Capsulectomy
points: Removes intact implant and capsule together
